conviction_note: A near non-result on a mega-cap with heavy coverage. The H1 (Mar-Aug) quarter was largely set on 2026-07-09: the H1 OP plan of 234bn was fixed after 7-Eleven Inc.'s Apr-Jun quarter had already closed. What is left is the FY decision. Peer fuel margins through July (Couche-Tard 52.61c, +8.61c; Casey's 47.8c, +6.8c) sit above the 'conservative' H2 fuel case behind SEI's H2 OP of $1,147m (-12.7% YoY), which argues for a raise. Against that, the street's ordinary-profit number of 402.2bn already sits 12bn above the plan, September brought record pump prices from rising crude (the setup that squeezes retail margins), and this name sold its last fuel-driven raise (-0.37% next day, then kept falling). So p_up is 52 on a 2.8% scale, giving +0.11. The findings sum to +0.40: the two measurements agree in sign, and the gap is the priced consensus raise, which pulls p_up to 50 more than it shrinks the fuel finding itself.
bar: Company H1 operating profit plan of 234.0bn yen and FY plan of 425.0bn OP / 390.0bn ordinary, revised 2026-07-09 (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260709/140120260708590082.pdf). Street FY ordinary-profit consensus is 402,225m yen per kabuyoho (https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/report?bcode=3382, data updated 2026-10-07). That is one source, so the street bar counts as single-sourced. Sizes are capped accordingly.
positioning_check: The JPX register sums to 6.87% (2 sellers, as of 2026-09-29), but 6.28% of that is SMBC Nikko's hedge for the 2026-08-03 accelerated share repurchase: 173.9m shares sold to the company via ToSTNeT-3 and covered steadily since, down to 145.8m shares by 09-29 (https://karauri.net/3382/; https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260803/140120260803506304.pdf). The rest is MUFG Morgan Stanley at 0.50%. This is a mechanical short being bought back on a VWAP schedule, not crowded short fuel, so the baseline's short_squeeze lean of +3.0 is spurious. 信用倍率 is 5.76x (kabutan, 2026-10-08), which leans long-heavy. There is no option skew in Japan. Run-up is -3.11% over 20 days and -1.18% over 5 days.

findings.finding: US fuel margins through July ran well above last year at the two peers that have reported (Couche-Tard US 52.61c/gal, +8.61c, 12 weeks to 2026-07-19; Casey's 47.8c, +6.8c, May-Jul). That is above the 'more conservative' H2 fuel case behind 7-Eleven Inc.'s H2 OP plan of $1,147m (-12.7% YoY, cut by $158m on 07-09), so the FY OP plan of 425bn has fuel upside that management will have seen through September by the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last fuel-driven raise (2026-07-09: H1 OP +23%, FY +4.9%) went -0.37% the next session and fell for four days ('surprise lacking', kabutan 2026-07-10). The last FY cut at H1 (2025-10-09) went -3.48%. So this name sells fuel-driven upgrades as one-offs.
findings.why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced. The street ordinary-profit number (402.2bn against 390bn) already carries about a 12bn raise, and the peer prints are public. What is not visible is how far September's record pump prices (AAA, Sept average $4.33) compressed SEI's Q3 margin against the strong Jun-Jul run-rate, and whether management passes the upside through or holds it back to 'reinvest' as it did in July. If the market had priced a large raise, the stock would not be down 3% over 20 days into the print.
findings.independence: Couche-Tard Q1 FY27 release (https://www.cantechletter.com/newswires/alimentation-couche-tard-announces-its-results-for-its-first-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2027/, 2026-09-01) and Casey's Q1 FY27 (https://pulse2.com/caseys-q1-eps-jumps-28-as-revenue-reaches-5-68-billion/, 2026-09-08) are independent of the company's document. AAA's October 1 note (https://gasprices.aaa.com/national-average-dips-following-record-setting-september/) cuts the other way for September.

findings.finding: Seven-Eleven Japan same-store sales slowed to 0.0% in June and +0.6% in July (customer counts -3.5% and -2.2%, late end to the rainy season), against +2.0% in Q1 and a FY plan of +2.5%. The domestic H2 plan (OP +3.0% YoY) is therefore at risk of a trim.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean isolated reaction to a domestic same-store miss in this name's history. SEJ is about half of H1 OP (120.4bn of 234bn plan).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the 月次 are public, and Q2 domestic OP is a few billion yen on a 234bn H1. It remains a finding only because it could become a domestic-segment guide trim at this print.
findings.independence: June figure: https://www.ryutsuu.biz/sales/s071083.html (same publisher, different month). The FY +2.5% plan is in the Q1 supplementary data (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260709/140120260708590072.pdf).

findings.finding: Of the 6.87% disclosed short, 6.28% is SMBC Nikko's hedge for the 367.3bn-yen accelerated repurchase of 2026-08-03. Nikko is covering it on a VWAP schedule (173.9m to 145.8m shares by 09-29). That is a steady mechanical bid through the window, not squeezable short interest.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history; the ASR began 2026-08-03 and the stock has drifted from about 2,105 to 1,976 while the cover ran.
findings.why_not_priced: The bid is known and runs daily, so its effect over one session is tiny. The point is that the baseline's +3.0 squeeze lean reads a hedge as crowded short interest, so nothing should be sized off that lean.
findings.independence: ASR terms in the company's own disclosure: https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260803/140120260803506304.pdf (2026-08-03).

outside_window.finding: The US IPO of 7-Eleven Inc. has been pushed to FY2027 at the earliest. The 2tn-yen buyback-plus-progressive-dividend commitment to FY2030 continues. Neither is dated inside this window.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: likely in play. The street FY ordinary profit (402.2bn) sits 3% above the plan (390bn), so holding the plan would disappoint mildly and a fuel-led raise is the upside. Returns: none expected; the 367bn ASR ran in August and the dividend is 60 yen (30 interim). New-year guide: not applicable at H1. Quarter: Q1 OP 105.0bn was 44.9% of the 234bn H1 plan, against 31.2% (65.1/208.4) last year, and SEI's H1 was fixed after its Apr-Jun quarter closed, so the H1 print should land at or slightly above plan.

baseline_tension: The baseline lean of +3.0 rests almost entirely on a short register that is really an ASR hedge, so the stock has no squeeze fuel. My small positive comes from fuel-driven guidance upside, not positioning. It runs against the 20-day drift (-3.1%) and against this name's habit of selling fuel-led raises. The strongest positive the release could carry is a FY OP raise on fuel; I looked for it, and the street already prices about 12bn of it.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on public 月次): the SEJ same-store finding went from -0.2 to -0.1, since the June/July figures are public and only a domestic guide trim would add to them; p_up was already near 50, so it stayed at 52.

Rule 2 (check the sign): negatives do not dominate here (one small negative against one positive and one neutral-positive). The strongest positive the release could carry is written into baseline_tension; nothing else moved.
